title: Stability figures ask whether an error mode grows or decays, and by how much per step
summary: Stability regions, amplification-factor curves, CFL sweeps and step-profile comparisons are four views of one idea: a numerical scheme multiplies each error mode by a factor every step. If that factor stays at or below one in size the run is stable; how far below one sets the numerical damping.

media.alt: Six panels titled FE, BE, CN, RK4, AB2 and BDF2 on axes of Re and Im of lambda times delta t from minus 4 to 2 and minus 4 to 4. The shaded stable region is a disc centred at minus 1 for FE, everything outside a disc centred at plus 1 for BE, the whole left half-plane for CN, a rounded region reaching about minus 2.8 on the real axis for RK4, a small region reaching minus 1 for AB2, and the outside of a large bulge on the right for BDF2.

source.caption: Numerical stability regions
group: 35_edu_08_numerical_diffusion: Numerical diffusion on a step profile with UDS, CDS, TVD minmod and TVD superbee
source.note: Group of four cfdcore numerics figures. The stability-region panel is the representative image; the other three are described in the teaching text. Values quoted are read from the figures or computed from the standard formulas shown.

read_the_figure.question: For which step sizes and wavelengths does the scheme keep errors bounded, and what does it do to the solution when it does?
read_the_figure.axes: Stability regions (representative figure): x is Re(lambda dt), y is Im(lambda dt), the complex number formed by the test-equation eigenvalue and the time step; shaded means stable. Von Neumann figure: x is the phase angle theta/pi of a Fourier mode (0 is the longest wave, 1 is the 2-cell zig-zag), y is |G|, the factor by which the mode amplitude changes per step, at CFL = 0.5. CFL sweep: x is CFL number, y is the maximum |phi| at t = 2 (a blow-up indicator). Numerical-diffusion figure: x is position, y is the advected quantity phi, for a step profile at t = 0, 0.5 and 1.0 (CFL = 0.45, 200 cells).
look_at: Regions: is the whole left half-plane shaded (A-stable: CN, BE, BDF2) or only a bounded patch (FE, RK4, AB2)? For BE and BDF2 the stable area is the outside of the white blob, so check which side is shaded.
Where a region crosses the real axis on the left it gives the largest lambda dt a stiff decay can take: about -2 for FE, about -2.8 for RK4, -1 for AB2.
Von Neumann curves: stay on or below the dashed line |G| = 1. Above it, a mode grows every step. Strictly below it, the mode is damped; the further below, the stronger the damping.
CFL sweep: blue dots are stable runs, red crosses would be unstable ones. Here only stable dots are drawn, up to CFL = 1, with the theoretical limit as a dashed line; nothing is plotted beyond it.
Step profile: compare each panel's front width with the sharp dashed initial condition, and look for overshoots beyond 0 and 1.
read_the_figure.proves: Each figure checks one implemented scheme against a known result of standard theory: the shape of its stability region, the formula for its amplification factor, the CFL limit, or the qualitative diffusion and oscillation behaviour. Agreement shows the scheme was coded as the theory describes. It does not show that the scheme is accurate for a given problem.
if_wrong: A region that differs from the textbook shape (for example a disc not touching the origin, or the wrong side shaded): a sign or coefficient error in the scheme's update formula, or in the plotting test.
|G| above one for a scheme theory says is stable: check the CFL used, the sign of the advection velocity, and the boundary treatment.
A CFL sweep that blows up well below the stated limit, or never blows up above it: the sweep may not be testing what its label says (different time integrator, too few steps for growth to show).
A step profile with ripples in a scheme that should be bounded: a limiter or flux-ratio bug.
must_check: State the test problem each time: lambda from u' = lambda u for regions, u_t + a u_x = 0 for Von Neumann and CFL.
Say which side is shaded, and give the real-axis intercept for each region.
State CFL, number of cells and time for every profile figure.
A sweep should show both stable and unstable points on each side of the limit; one-sided evidence cannot locate the limit.
Unreadable annotations are a defect: the CDS panel in the step-profile figure overprints its own transition-width label.
as_drawn: Regions (read off the plot): FE is a disc of radius 1 centred at -1, real-axis limit -2. RK4 reaches about -2.8 on the real axis and about 2.9 on the imaginary axis. AB2 reaches -1 on the real axis. CN is exactly the left half-plane. BE and BDF2 are stable outside a bounded region in the right half-plane.

Von Neumann at CFL = 0.5: UDS+FE falls to 0 at theta = pi; CDS+FE rises above one, peaking near 1.12 at theta = pi/2; CDS+CN lies on |G| = 1; UDS+CN ends near 0.33 and UDS+RK4 near 0.375 at theta = pi. These end values agree with the closed forms (1-2c), (1-c)/(1+c) and the RK4 polynomial at z = -2c, computed in Apply.
CFL sweep: the dots are all stable, between CFL 0.2 and 1.0, with max |phi| rising slowly from about 0.6 to 1.0. No unstable points are drawn.

Step profile: printed transition widths are 0.130 (UDS), 0.010 (TVD minmod) and 0.005 (TVD superbee); the CDS panel shows grid-scale oscillations filling the whole axis and its width label is illegible.

terms.meaning: u' = lambda u with complex lambda. Every linear stability result for time integrators is stated as a condition on the single number lambda dt.
The number G by which one step multiplies the amplitude of a mode: u_{n+1} = G u_n. Stability needs |G| <= 1.
The set of complex z = lambda dt for which |G(z)| <= 1.
The stability region contains the whole left half-plane, so any decaying mode is stepped stably at any step size. BE and CN have this property; FE and RK4 do not.
The distance a wave travels in one step, measured in cells: c = a dt / dx.
Insert a single Fourier mode e^{i j theta} into a linear scheme and read off G(theta); theta = k dx is the phase advance per cell.
Upwind (first order, one-sided), central (second order) and total-variation-diminishing limited schemes (minmod, superbee), which switch between the two to avoid new extrema.
Smearing produced by the truncation error of a scheme, which acts like an extra diffusion term in the modified equation.

remember: Stability is about the growth factor of each mode: |G| <= 1 for every mode that the grid can hold.
Explicit Euler on u' = lambda u is stable for |1 + lambda dt| <= 1: the disc of radius 1 centred at -1.
Upwind with forward Euler is stable for 0 <= c <= 1; central with forward Euler is unstable at every c > 0 because |G|^2 = 1 + c^2 sin^2 theta.
Stability is not accuracy: BE is stable everywhere in the left half-plane yet only first order, and a stable upwind run smears fronts.
A figure of a stability limit needs points on both sides of the limit.

understand.title: Four figures, one mechanism
understand.text: The regions say what a time integrator does to one decaying or oscillating mode. The Von Neumann curves say what a space-plus-time scheme does to each wavelength of an advected wave. The CFL sweep is the experiment that tests the resulting limit in a real run, and the step profile shows the visible consequence of the damping and dispersion that remain inside the stable range.

understand.title: Reading a region
understand.text: Place your lambda dt on the plane. A decaying physical mode has lambda on the negative real axis; an oscillation has lambda on the imaginary axis; a damped oscillation is in between. Stability asks whether that point is shaded. A stiff problem has lambda dt far to the left for any reasonable dt, which is why only schemes with a left-half-plane region (CN, BE, BDF2) are used for stiff systems.

understand.title: Stable is not faithful
understand.text: CN is stable for every decaying mode but has |G| near -1 for very stiff ones, so it does not damp them, while BE damps them strongly. On the Von Neumann plot the same split appears: CDS+CN sits exactly at |G| = 1, so it keeps every wave and is dissipation-free but oscillation-prone, and UDS curves fall steeply for short waves, which is the numerical diffusion visible in the step-profile panel.

steps.title: Amplification factor of explicit Euler
steps.note: This is a disc of radius 1 centred at z = -1, the FE panel. Its real-axis limit is z = -2.

steps.title: Implicit Euler and Crank-Nicolson
steps.note: BE has |G| <= 1 outside the disc of radius 1 centred at +1, which is the shaded area of the BE panel. CN has |G| <= 1 exactly when Re z <= 0, the left half-plane.

steps.title: Fourier mode in space
steps.note: Substituting a single mode into a linear constant-coefficient scheme turns the difference equation into an algebraic equation for G(theta). theta = pi is the shortest wave, alternating sign on neighbouring cells.

steps.title: Upwind with forward Euler
steps.note: For 0 <= c <= 1 the correction term is non-negative, so |G| <= 1. At c = 0.5 and theta = pi, G = 1 - 2c = 0, the blue curve ending at zero. For c > 1 the factor 1-c is negative and |G| exceeds one at theta = pi: the CFL limit.

steps.title: Central with forward Euler
steps.note: |G| is greater than one for every wave except theta = 0 and pi, at every c: the orange curve. At c = 0.5 and theta = pi/2 it is sqrt(1.25), about 1.118, which is the visible peak.

steps.title: Modified equation of upwind
steps.note: Taylor expansion of the upwind update shows an extra diffusion term. It is first order in dx, which is why the upwind front is smeared and why refining the grid narrows it only slowly.

steps.title: Width of a diffused front
steps.note: A step diffusing with coefficient nu spreads as an error function of standard deviation sigma, and the 10 to 90 percent width is about 2.56 sigma. The Apply section turns this into a number for the UDS panel.

worked.title: Predict the UDS front width in the step-profile panel
worked.problem: The panel uses a = 1 (the front crosses the unit domain in t = 1), 200 cells, CFL c = 0.45, and is read at t = 1. Estimate the 10 to 90 percent transition width and compare with the printed 0.130.

solution.text: Grid spacing and numerical diffusion coefficient from the modified equation.

worked.answer: About 0.13, in good agreement with the printed 0.130. The upwind smearing is explained by the modified-equation diffusion alone.

analyze.q: Why does the CDS panel oscillate across the whole domain while the FE CDS curve exceeds one only by about 12 percent per step?
analyze.hint: Growth compounds over hundreds of steps: 1.12 to the power n.

analyze.q: The CFL sweep shows no unstable points. What can and cannot be concluded about the limit CFL = 1?
analyze.hint: A limit needs evidence on both sides.

analyze.q: CN is A-stable but UDS+CN in the Von Neumann plot still damps short waves. Where does that damping come from?
analyze.hint: Compare CDS+CN, which does not damp.

evaluate.q: Would you choose BE or CN for a very stiff, smooth problem where you care about the long-time decay?
evaluate.hint: Compare their |G| as lambda dt goes to minus infinity.

evaluate.q: Which of the four panels in the step-profile figure would you accept for a front that must stay between 0 and 1, and what do you give up?
evaluate.hint: Boundedness versus smearing, and the cost of a limiter.

create: Redraw the CFL sweep with both stable and unstable points: run CFL from 0.2 to 1.5 and mark any run with max |phi| above its initial maximum.
Add a contour of |G| = 1 for CDS+FE and UDS+FE in the (c, theta) plane to show where each is stable.

checks.q: What does it mean for a point lambda dt to lie inside a stability region?
checks.answer: The amplification factor satisfies |G| <= 1 there, so the mode that point represents does not grow from step to step.

checks.q: Explicit Euler is applied to u' = -50 u. What is the largest stable step?
checks.hint: Real-axis limit of the FE region is -2.

checks.q: UDS+FE has G = 0 at theta = pi for CFL = 0.5 and CDS+CN has |G| = 1 everywhere. Which will smear a step and which will ring?
checks.hint: Short waves are what make a sharp front.
checks.answer: UDS+FE damps the shortest waves completely and so smears the front; CDS+CN keeps every wave at full amplitude, so the short waves it generates at a step do not decay and it rings.

checks.q: A CFL sweep shows only stable runs up to CFL = 1. Is the limit confirmed?
checks.hint: What would an unstable run show?
checks.answer: No. It shows that nothing failed up to 1, but not that runs beyond 1 fail; unstable points above the limit are needed to locate it.

checks.q: How would you test a new scheme's stability region numerically?
checks.answer: Apply the scheme to u' = lambda u over a grid of complex z = lambda dt values (or evaluate G(z) analytically), mark |G| <= 1, and compare the contour with the theoretical region, especially the real-axis intercept.
